chunks: And Samāʿah ibn Mihrān narrated from Abū Baṣīr, from Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said:
There is no harm in the testimony of a guest if he is chaste and trustworthy.
He said: The testimony of an employee for his employer is disliked, but there is no harm in his testimony for someone else, and there is no harm in it for him after his separation from him.

key_terms.الضَّيْفِ: a guest whose testimony is being considered
key_terms.شَهَادَةِ: testimony given in a legal or judicial context
key_terms.صَائِنًا: trustworthy and protective of his integrity
key_terms.صَاحِبِهِ: his employer or the one who hired him
key_terms.عَفِيفًا: chaste and restrained from improper conduct
key_terms.مُفَارَقَتِهِ: his separation or departure from the employment relationship

ai.seo_question: When is the testimony of a guest or employee accepted in Islamic law?
ai.summary: This hadith gives legal guidance on the acceptance of testimony in judicial matters. It states that a guest's testimony is acceptable when he is chaste and trustworthy, while the testimony of an employee for his employer is regarded as disliked due to possible partiality, though it is acceptable for others and after the employment relationship has ended.
